text:
elaine: ran the quantization + concurrency sweep overnight against model-x-v2. p95 latency looks fine at low qps but cost/token for int8 is ~18% higher than bf16 at 64 concurrency. sketch of runs attached (see below).
jonas: ugh. did you pin the same sequence length distribution? sometimes the warmup/kv cache makes token accounting look off.
elaine: yes pinned seq=1024, same prompt corpus. samples:
```
> bf16 run: qps=150, p95=82ms, cost_token=$0.00082
> int8 run: qps=150, p95=89ms, cost_token=$0.00097
```
raf: can we confirm the cost calculation is measuring emitted tokens only and not input tokens + system tokens? we've had mismatches before.
elaine: cost calc is using the eval harness metric token_cost = total_spent / emitted_tokens. logs show total_spent delta too, not just emitted_tokens.
sam: share the runner config used for int8? maybe batching window different or there was more queuing.
elaine: posted runner args:
```
--runner=runner-v3 
--batch_window_ms=12 
--concurrency=64 
--quant=dynamic-int8
--kv_prefetch=true
```
jonas: batch_window=12 is higher than our usual 8 for these models. that can increase per-token latency but cost? hmm. also runner-v3 had a reorder patch last week for prefetchtasks. could be a telemetry bug where cost attribution runs on a per-request basis but the runner charges per-batch.
perf-bot: nightly-eval model-x-v2 int8 sweep finished. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/1907504321/int8/ (metrics.csv, traces.zip).
elaine: I grabbed the traces. noticed a pattern: first 30s of each worker have high token issuance (warmup) and we seem to double-charge the same tokens when KV prefetch pipeline overlaps with batching boundary. snippet from trace:
```
[worker-12] emit_tokens: 1200
[worker-12] billed_tokens: 2400  <-- suspicious
```
raf: that sounds like an ordering bug in the accounting hook. maybe we increment billed_tokens at request start and again at commit if prefetch finishes after batch flush.
jonas: I can repro locally with a short harness. patch idea: make accounting idempotent per request_id and only commit billed_tokens once on finalization. minimal change in runner-v3.
sam: if we change runner behavior, CI needs a test. currently we only assert total_throughput and p95, not token accounting. that's probably why this slipped.
elaine: creating a new CI test: submit a synthetic warmup-heavy workload and assert billed_tokens == emitted_tokens within 1%. will add to eng-ml CI job that runs on PRs to runner.
ci-bot: created issue #4528: "runner: idempotent billing hook for prefetch+batching overlap" and attached failing trace.
jonas: I'll prepare a small patch and include a unit harness reproducer. will also add a telemetry flag log.acct_request_id to make debugging easier.
raf: also update dashboards: add "billed / emitted tokens" ratio to eval-run dashboard so we can alert when >1.05.
elaine: agreed. right now dashboard shows cost/token and p95; add ratio and a histogram for per-worker skew.
sam: re: rollouts - gate the change behind a feature flag for dedicated clusters first. safer to flip for hosted after a week of smoke.
elaine: open question: does quantization amplify the overlap because int8 runs faster per-op and shifts timing? I think yes — earlier batch boundaries and prefetch completion interplay differently. we should run a quick A/B with identical batching windows and a controlled synthetic qps.
jonas: timeline: patch + unit test today, CI integration test tomorrow, dashboard + alert Friday, canary rollout next week.
elaine: adding todo: rerun overnight sweep after patch and paste new metrics here. tagging @jonas @sam @raf for follow-up. :thumbsup:
